desc: Parse input: N and the N×N character grid; build adjacency structures.
Precompute in_edges[v][c] and out_edges[u][c] bucketed by character.
Initialize dist matrix with 0 for (i,i) and 1 for direct edges; seed BFS queue (0-level first, then 1-level).
BFS with +2 wrap transitions using character-bucketed adjacency; verify queue monotonicity (seeds ordered 0 then 1, all steps +2 ⇒ FIFO order is nondecreasing, so first visit is optimal).
Print the dist matrix in required format.

Write the complete Python solution: parse input, build per-character in/out adjacency lists, run the multi-source BFS over (u,v) state pairs with 0/1 seeds and +2 transitions, and print the resulting distance matrix.
Sanity-check the code mentally against both samples (e.g., sample 1: (1,4)=4 via abba; sample 2: (5,3)=5).
